_readme: Plan-map data. One entry per topic. Ten-second capture: append {id,title,campaign,status} — wire deps/links later. Viewer: /Aralia/planmap/index.html on any dev server. status: parked | specced | active | done. deps: ids this topic REQUIRES. A dep may also carry `feature: <slug>` to narrow the arrow to ONE feature of the target topic (slug = that feature's title run through the same slugifier as the ids); the `why` still explains the edge, the pointer is now structural. link: repo-relative spec doc path (opened via the dev server's /@fs bridge using repoRoot). Truth-ownership + promotion rules (who owns statuses/decisions/deps; gaps flow UP by human curation only, plan flows DOWN via planmap-to-wave): tools/agora/PLANNING-STACK.md. `open`: integer mirror of the linked subspec's '## Open' bullet count (recompute when the doc changes — it is NOT invented, it is counted). `spike: true`: research that could invalidate the approach (dashed ⚠ tile). status also allows 'superseded' (dead decision — drops to the Graveyard strip; add a one-line `killed` reason). `focus: true` on at most ONE topic = what Remy is actually touching now (★ FOCUS). Freshness fields (2026-07-14 design): `updated` (YYYY-MM-DD, tooling-written date of last real change), `tier` (strategic | component, optional), `status_note` (free-text nuance, topics and features), `decision` (boolean on features: true = waiting on human call).

The sheet already carries that per vertex, so the transmission chunk is hand-expanded and its thickness line repointed at it. Caustics ported from the battle map, weighted to the shallows because caustics are light that reached the bottom. FOUR faults found and fixed, all by capture: the albedo painted depth a second time on top of Beer law (near-black lake); the absorption distance was 3.2 m on water five metres and deeper, which makes a transmitting surface look identical to a non-transmitting one (Hall of Shame 15); a pale self-lit emissive tuned for an opaque surface washed over the refracted scene; and transmission replaces alpha blending, so the shallow fringe drew solid until thin water was dropped outright below 3 cm. THE FINDING THAT MATTERS BEYOND THIS LOOK: on the same 44,331 m3 lake, the two judged looks draw 9.9 percent of the frame as water and this one draws 23-34 percent. Their opacity ramps start at 0.14 at the shore and most of a lake AREA is shallow, so from overhead a large lake is nearly invisible in both. Open: reflections of sky and shore.

features.title: Ripples driven by their causes: twenty-three signatures, two of them derived
features.note: Remy picked seven in round 3, six more in round 4, and all ten of the next batch in round 5 — so the list grew by his choice rather than by curation. Each carries size, strength, decay and repeat, argued from what the event physically IS rather than tuned by eye, because eye-tuning failed twice: rain came out thirty times too hard, and a spell reached 10.9 m because repeated pushes at ONE cell resonate. Six causes LIFT the surface (wind, bubbles, boil, swimmer, surfacing, partWater) and a test names them, so a dropped minus sign still fails. TWO ARE DERIVED and nobody places them: rapids where the Froude number is high, and the hydraulic jump where it CROSSES one — a two-cell test, not a threshold, because a uniformly supercritical field is all rapids and no jump. The deck groups them by behaviour: press once, keep running, and the solver finds these. 24 unit tests.

features.note: Aims at the depth-weighted centre of the whole wet set, sized by its spread, and always above the terrain — a camera placed relative to the WATER ended up inside the hillside. Reports "sunk N m below the land" when the pool is under the rim, which is the honest answer on the sandbox cell.

features.title: Liquid skin for the land droplets: a screen-space fluid surface, written for WebGL2
features.note: Remy called the droplets ugly, and on this page they were THREE.Points sprites — so you saw balls. Now they are drawn as spheres into a depth buffer, that depth is smoothed with a narrow-range filter, and the result is shaded as a surface. Written for WebGL2: flipSurfaceRender.ts does the same job in TSL on three/webgpu and none of its code carries across. The ground is drawn depth-only into the same targets, so terrain occludes the water without a copy of the scene. Sprites stay one click away on the same water. Three faults found and fixed, all by looking rather than by measuring: a linear colour written straight to the screen (black lumps), a filter sized in pixels for a subject sized in metres (2 m droplets projecting to 58 px against a 12 px kernel), and a one-pixel checkerboard from a per-pixel choice between forward and backward differences. Hall of Shame entries 12, 13 and 14. Open: refraction, and a performance reading.

features.title: See-through water is the DEFAULT, and it only costs when there is water
features.note: Remy round 5 q16 chose it; round 6 q18 asked to stop paying for it on frames with no water, and round 6 q17 confirmed the PHYSICAL read is what he wants — shallow water shows the bed. The cost is three own transmission pass, a second render of the opaque scene, which it runs whenever a visible un-culled object carries transmission. So the frame loop hides the sheet when its draw range is zero, and recomputes the bounding sphere so frustum culling can answer the in-frame half honestly. No material swaps class per frame. The measurement that settled q17: on the SAME 210,368 pixels, sandbox reads rgb(40,87,99) at 60 percent saturation and see-through reads rgb(79,84,74) at 12 percent, passing about twice the red — which is the lake bed, visible through six metres of water. The older looks go opaque within two metres, so they call almost any water deep. One is stylised, one is physical, and Remy picked physical.
